title: 计算机科学，从零搭建 · 第44部分：人与产品

chapters.Choice: 2. 选择，以及预测一项任务的用时
chapters.Cuped: 10. 更少的噪声，同样的真相
chapters.Outro: 回顾、习题，以及它们会在哪里再出现

8138bd6877be.en: On the ninth of December 1968, in San Francisco, Douglas Engelbart sat on a stage with a screen, a keyboard and a small wooden box with wheels underneath. <bookmark mark='a'/> For ninety minutes he showed a thousand engineers what a computer could be for a person. A pointer on the screen that followed his hand, through the box his lab had invented: the mouse. <bookmark mark='b'/> Words linked to other words, so that clicking one opened another: hypertext. <bookmark mark='c'/> A colleague thirty miles away, editing the same document at the same time, <bookmark mark='d'/> his face in a window on the screen. <bookmark mark='e'/> It was one working system, called NLS, from Engelbart's lab at the Stanford Research Institute. It came to be called the mother of all demos.
8138bd6877be.zh: 1968年12月9日，在旧金山，Douglas Engelbart 坐在一个舞台上，面前是一块屏幕、一个键盘，还有一个底下装着轮子的小木盒。<bookmark mark='a'/>在九十分钟里，他向一千名工程师展示了计算机能为一个人做些什么。屏幕上有一个指针，跟着他的手移动，靠的就是他的实验室发明的那个盒子：鼠标。<bookmark mark='b'/>文字链接到别的文字，点击一处就打开另一处：超文本。<bookmark mark='c'/>一位远在三十英里外的同事，同时编辑着同一份文档，<bookmark mark='d'/>他的脸出现在屏幕上的一个窗口里。<bookmark mark='e'/>这是一个完整可用的系统，叫作 NLS，出自 Engelbart 在斯坦福研究所的实验室。后来，人们称它为“演示之母”。

bd8c6245e19c.en: The ideas took fifteen years to reach ordinary desks. <bookmark mark='a'/> At Xerox PARC, the Alto of 1973 put windows, icons and a mouse on a personal machine. In 1979 Steve Jobs visited, and the Macintosh followed in 1984, Windows a year later. The web arrived in 1991, and multi-touch phones in 2007. <bookmark mark='b'/> Each step was an argument about people: what they can see, reach, remember and decide, and how quickly. This part treats those arguments as science.
bd8c6245e19c.zh: 这些想法花了十五年，才走上普通人的办公桌。<bookmark mark='a'/>在施乐帕洛阿尔托研究中心（Xerox PARC），1973年的 Alto 把窗口、图标和鼠标放到了一台个人计算机上。1979年，乔布斯（Steve Jobs）前去参观，随后在1984年有了 Macintosh，一年之后有了 Windows。万维网在1991年到来，多点触控手机在2007年到来。<bookmark mark='b'/>每一步都是一场关于人的争论：人能看到什么、够到什么、记住什么、决定什么，以及有多快。这一部分把这些争论当作科学来对待。

08c219253358.en: Two kinds of measurement run through this part. <bookmark mark='a'/> The first is of people. The time to point at a target grows with the logarithm of its distance over its width, so precisely that the points fall on a line. That is Fitts's law, and it comes from Shannon's channel capacity. <bookmark mark='b'/> The second is of products: controlled experiments that compare two versions with real users. They have their own traps. Here, two identical versions are compared and checked every day for a month; 28 percent of these experiments declare a winner where there is none, against the five percent the test promises.
08c219253358.zh: 贯穿这一部分的有两种测量。<bookmark mark='a'/>第一种测量的是人。指向一个目标所用的时间，随它的距离与宽度之比的对数增长，精确到所有的点都落在一条直线上。这就是 Fitts 定律，它来自香农的信道容量。<bookmark mark='b'/>第二种测量的是产品：用真实用户比较两个版本的对照实验。它们有自己的陷阱。这里，我们比较两个完全相同的版本，一个月里每天检查一次；这样的实验中有28%宣布了一个其实并不存在的赢家，而检验承诺的只有5%。

31f2ba38a25e.en: This is Part 44 of Computer Science, Built, the last part of Act Eight. <bookmark mark='a'/> We will derive Fitts's law from channel capacity and Hick's law from entropy; predict how long a task takes before anyone does it; turn colour into formulas and check this series' own palette for colour-blind viewers; and then run experiments on products, deriving their power, and seeing why looking at the results every morning breaks them, and how to look safely.
31f2ba38a25e.zh: 这是计算机科学，从零搭建，第44部分，也是第八幕的最后一部分。<bookmark mark='a'/>我们将从信道容量推导出 Fitts 定律，从熵推导出 Hick 定律；在任何人动手之前，预测一项任务要花多长时间；把颜色变成公式，并为色盲观众检查这个系列自己的调色板；然后在产品上做实验，推导它们的统计功效，看清为什么每天早上查看结果会破坏实验，以及怎样安全地查看。

5916c1cf2c3f.en: Chapter one. Pointing is a channel.
5916c1cf2c3f.zh: 第一章：指点是一条信道。

3746695e4a09.en: In 1954 the psychologist Paul Fitts asked people to tap a metal stylus back and forth between two plates, as fast as they could without missing. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each plate has a width, and the two are a distance apart. <bookmark mark='b'/> Move the plates farther apart, or make them narrower, and the taps slow down. Doubling the distance costs about as much as halving the width: only the ratio of distance to width matters, and the time grows with its logarithm. He had been reading Shannon, and he called his paper the information capacity of the human motor system.
3746695e4a09.zh: 1954年，心理学家 Paul Fitts 让人们拿着一支金属触笔，在两块金属板之间来回敲击，在不失手的前提下越快越好。<bookmark mark='a'/>每块板有一个宽度，两块板之间隔着一段距离。<bookmark mark='b'/>把两块板移得更远，或者把它们做得更窄，敲击就会变慢。距离加倍的代价，大约和宽度减半相同：只有距离与宽度之比才要紧，而时间随这个比值的对数增长。他当时正在读香农，于是把论文题为《人类运动系统的信息容量》。

40ea9480be98.en: Fitts's analogy was Shannon's channel capacity from Part 28. <bookmark mark='a'/> A channel's capacity in bits grows with the logarithm of one plus signal over noise. <bookmark mark='b'/> In pointing, the distance plays the signal and the width the noise the movement may tolerate. The index of difficulty, log of distance over width plus one, counts the bits a movement must deliver. This is Scott MacKenzie's form from 1992; it never goes negative, and it fits better than Fitts's original. <bookmark mark='c'/> Movement time is then a constant, for starting and stopping, plus a slope times the bits. The slope is seconds per bit, and its inverse is a throughput: the bandwidth of a hand.
40ea9480be98.zh: Fitts 的类比，是第28部分讲过的香农信道容量。<bookmark mark='a'/>一条信道以比特计的容量，随一加信噪比的对数增长。<bookmark mark='b'/>在指点中，距离扮演信号，宽度扮演这次运动所能容忍的噪声。难度指数，即距离除以宽度再加一的对数，数的是一次运动必须传递的比特数。这是 Scott MacKenzie 在1992年给出的形式；它永远不会是负数，而且比 Fitts 的原始形式拟合得更好。<bookmark mark='c'/>于是，运动时间等于一个常数，用于启动和停止，再加上斜率乘以比特数。斜率的单位是秒每比特，它的倒数是一个吞吐量：一只手的带宽。

6c68d7caa59c.en: Why a logarithm? David Meyer and colleagues, in 1988, gave an answer. <bookmark mark='a'/> A movement is a series of submovements. Each aims at the centre of the target and lands with an error proportional to the distance it covered; if it misses, another follows. <bookmark mark='b'/> So each correction shrinks the remaining distance by a roughly constant factor, and the number of corrections grows with the logarithm of distance over width. <bookmark mark='c'/> We simulated that hand on twenty targets, near and far, wide and narrow. <bookmark mark='d'/> The points fall on a line, with R squared of 0.99. The slope is 0.086 seconds per bit: a throughput of 11.6 bits per second for our simulated hand. People measured with a mouse manage a few bits per second, according to Soukoreff and MacKenzie in 2004.
6c68d7caa59c.zh: 为什么是对数？David Meyer 和同事们在1988年给出了一个答案。<bookmark mark='a'/>一次运动是一连串子运动。每一次都瞄准目标的中心，落点的误差与它走过的距离成正比；如果没打中，就再来一次。<bookmark mark='b'/>所以每次修正，都把剩余的距离缩小一个大致固定的倍数，修正的次数就随距离与宽度之比的对数增长。<bookmark mark='c'/>我们在二十个目标上模拟了这只手，有近有远，有宽有窄。<bookmark mark='d'/>这些点落在一条直线上，R 平方为0.99。斜率是每比特0.086秒：我们这只模拟的手，吞吐量是每秒11.6比特。据 Soukoreff 和 MacKenzie 2004年的研究，人们用鼠标测得的吞吐量是每秒几比特。

d394f06c0ffa.en: Designers exploit a loophole. <bookmark mark='a'/> A pointer cannot leave the screen. Aim at a target on the edge and overshoot is impossible: the pointer stops there, as if the target were infinitely deep. <bookmark mark='b'/> In our simulation the same target takes 0.77 seconds in the middle and 0.40 at the edge: the hand can fling, and need not correct. <bookmark mark='c'/> That is why the Macintosh, in 1984, put a single menu bar at the very top of the screen, and why the corners, edges twice over, are the fastest places of all to reach.
d394f06c0ffa.zh: 设计师会利用一个漏洞。<bookmark mark='a'/>指针不能离开屏幕。瞄准屏幕边缘上的目标，就不可能冲过头：指针会停在那里，就好像目标无限深。<bookmark mark='b'/>在我们的模拟中，同一个目标放在中间要0.77秒，放在边缘只要0.40秒：手可以一甩而过，不必修正。<bookmark mark='c'/>这就是为什么1984年的 Macintosh 把唯一的菜单栏放在屏幕的最顶端，也是为什么角落，相当于两重边缘，是所有地方中最快能到达的。

109bb342a4a0.en: Some movements must stay inside a path. <bookmark mark='a'/> To reach a submenu, the pointer travels along the parent item, and if it slips out on the way the submenu closes. <bookmark mark='b'/> Johnny Accot and Shumin Zhai showed in 1997 that steering through a tunnel takes time proportional to its length over its width, summed along the path. That is linear, not logarithmic, so tunnels cost far more than targets. <bookmark mark='c'/> Nested menus are tunnels in series. The remedies are wider items, shallower menus, and submenus that forgive a diagonal path towards them.
109bb342a4a0.zh: 有些运动必须保持在一条路径之内。<bookmark mark='a'/>要到达一个子菜单，指针得沿着父菜单项移动，如果途中滑了出去，子菜单就会关闭。<bookmark mark='b'/>Johnny Accot 和 Shumin Zhai 在1997年证明，穿过一条隧道所需的时间，与它的长度除以宽度成正比，并沿着路径累加。这是线性的，不是对数的，所以隧道的代价比目标大得多。<bookmark mark='c'/>嵌套菜单就是串联起来的隧道。补救办法是：更宽的菜单项、更浅的菜单，以及能容忍指针斜着朝它们移动的子菜单。

1568904c6726.en: Chapter two. Choosing, and predicting how long a task will take.
1568904c6726.zh: 第二章：选择，以及预测一项任务的用时。

c877485d0369.en: In 1952 William Hick lit one of several lamps and timed how long people took to press the key beneath it. Reaction time grew with the logarithm of the number of lamps plus one, the one counting the chance that no lamp lit at all. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here is a chooser who halves the candidates with each comparison, the binary search of Part 16. Seven lamps and the chance of none make eight possibilities, and three comparisons find any of them. <bookmark mark='b'/> We simulated that chooser, at a fifth of a second to start and about 0.15 seconds per comparison, for one to ten lamps. Time against bits is a line, with R squared of 0.999: each bit of uncertainty costs the same.
c877485d0369.zh: 1952年，William Hick 点亮若干盏灯中的一盏，测量人们按下灯下方的按键要用多长时间。反应时间随灯的数目加一的对数增长，那个“一”算的是一盏灯都不亮的可能。<bookmark mark='a'/>这里有一个选择者，每做一次比较，就把候选项减半，也就是第16部分的二分查找。七盏灯，加上一盏都不亮的可能，一共八种可能，三次比较就能找到其中任意一种。<bookmark mark='b'/>我们模拟了这个选择者，启动要五分之一秒，每次比较大约0.15秒，灯从一盏到十盏。时间对比特数是一条直线，R 平方为0.999：每一比特的不确定性，代价都一样。

8b976b8f0b29.en: A year later Ray Hyman made the choices unequally likely, and reaction time followed the entropy of the choice rather than the number of options. <bookmark mark='a'/> Take a menu whose first item is chosen seventy percent of the time. Its entropy is 1.46 bits, against 2.32 for five equal choices. <bookmark mark='b'/> The best way to ask yes or no questions starts with the likely item: one question settles seventy percent of cases, and three settle the rest, <bookmark mark='c'/> 1.6 questions on average. That is the Huffman code of AI, Built Part 1, and it is never shorter than the entropy. The design rule follows: put the likely choice first, or make it the default.
8b976b8f0b29.zh: 一年之后，Ray Hyman 让各个选项出现的可能性不再相等，结果反应时间跟随的是这次选择的熵，而不是选项的个数。<bookmark mark='a'/>拿一个菜单来说，它的第一项有70%的时候被选中。它的熵是1.46比特，而五个等可能的选项是2.32比特。<bookmark mark='b'/>提是非题的最佳方式，是从最可能的那一项问起：一个问题就解决了70%的情况，再用三个问题解决其余的，<bookmark mark='c'/>平均1.6个问题。这正是《人工智能，从零搭建》第1部分的哈夫曼编码，它永远不会比熵更短。设计准则随之而来：把最可能的选项放在最前面，或者把它设为默认。

f827ce6905ab.en: Hick's law is often stretched too far. <bookmark mark='a'/> It describes choices you must decide among, when you already know the options. <bookmark mark='b'/> Reading an unfamiliar menu item by item is a search, and search time grows with the number of items, not with its logarithm. <bookmark mark='c'/> And practice flattens the slope: an expert who knows where everything is no longer chooses at all, but simply points.
f827ce6905ab.zh: Hick 定律常常被引申得太远。<bookmark mark='a'/>它描述的是：当你已经知道有哪些选项时，必须在其中做出的决定。<bookmark mark='b'/>逐项阅读一个不熟悉的菜单，是一种搜索，搜索时间随项数增长，而不是随它的对数增长。<bookmark mark='c'/>而且，练习会让斜率变平：一个知道每样东西在哪里的专家，根本不再选择，而是直接指过去。

21bdef35bc86.en: Stuart Card, Thomas Moran and Allen Newell turned these laws into an engineering tool. <bookmark mark='a'/> Their GOMS analysis describes a task as a goal, such as deleting a file; <bookmark mark='b'/> methods that achieve it, each a sequence of elementary operators: reach for the mouse, point, click, press a key; <bookmark mark='c'/> and selection rules for choosing between methods. Give every operator a time, and you can predict how long a task will take before anyone has built it.
21bdef35bc86.zh: Stuart Card、Thomas Moran 和 Allen Newell 把这些定律变成了一种工程工具。<bookmark mark='a'/>他们的 GOMS 分析把一项任务描述为：一个目标，比如删除一个文件；<bookmark mark='b'/>实现目标的方法，每种方法是一串基本操作符：伸手去拿鼠标、指向、点击、按一个键；<bookmark mark='c'/>以及在方法之间做选择的选择规则。给每个操作符一个时间，你就能在任何人把它造出来之前，预测一项任务要花多长时间。

3031849becb6.en: The keystroke-level model, which Card, Moran and Newell published in 1980, is the simplest version; the button press was added in later guides by David Kieras. <bookmark mark='a'/> A keystroke takes 0.28 seconds for an average typist, pointing with a mouse 1.1, a button press a tenth, moving a hand between keyboard and mouse 0.4, and a moment of mental preparation 1.35. <bookmark mark='b'/> Write each method as a string of operators and add them up. Deleting a file through a menu: 5.5 seconds. With a shortcut: 5.26. <bookmark mark='c'/> Renaming through a dialog: 9.47; inline: 8.85. <bookmark mark='d'/> The yellow blocks are moments of thought, and they dominate. A faster design is usually one that asks for fewer decisions, not fewer keys.
3031849becb6.zh: 击键层次模型（keystroke-level model）由 Card、Moran 和 Newell 在1980年发表，是最简单的版本；按下按钮这一项，是 David Kieras 后来在指南里加上的。<bookmark mark='a'/>对一个普通打字者来说，一次击键要0.28秒，用鼠标指向要1.1秒，按一下按钮要十分之一秒，把手在键盘和鼠标之间移动要0.4秒，片刻的心理准备要1.35秒。<bookmark mark='b'/>把每种方法写成一串操作符，再把它们加起来。通过菜单删除一个文件：5.5秒。用快捷键：5.26秒。<bookmark mark='c'/>通过对话框重命名：9.47秒；在原处直接重命名：8.85秒。<bookmark mark='d'/>黄色的方块是思考的时刻，它们占了大头。更快的设计，通常是要求更少决定的设计，而不是要求更少按键的设计。

6ac3dc3ae8e0.en: Chapter three. Perception and its thresholds.

0f7622412073.en: The first thresholds are in time. In 1968 Robert Miller, at IBM, asked how fast a computer must answer a person, and the answer has been restated ever since, by Card, Robertson and Mackinlay in 1991 and by Jakob Nielsen in 1993. <bookmark mark='a'/> Under a tenth of a second, a response feels instantaneous: the result itself is all the feedback needed. <bookmark mark='b'/> Under a second, the delay is noticed, but the user's flow of thought is not broken. <bookmark mark='c'/> Under ten seconds, attention holds, if the interface shows that work is happening. <bookmark mark='d'/> Beyond that, people turn away: show real progress, and let them do something else.
0f7622412073.zh: 第一类阈值在时间上。1968年，IBM 的 Robert Miller 问：计算机必须多快地回应一个人？此后，这个答案被一再重述：1991年由 Card、Robertson 和 Mackinlay，1993年由 Jakob Nielsen。<bookmark mark='a'/>不到十分之一秒，响应感觉是瞬时的：结果本身就是所需的全部反馈。<bookmark mark='b'/>不到一秒，延迟会被察觉，但用户的思路不会被打断。<bookmark mark='c'/>不到十秒，注意力还能维持，前提是界面表明工作正在进行。<bookmark mark='d'/>超过这个时间，人们就会转身离开：要显示真实的进度，并让他们去做别的事。

5ce2d01ee066.en: Direct manipulation is stricter than a tenth of a second. <bookmark mark='a'/> When you drag something under your finger, any delay shows as a gap between the finger and the thing. In 2012 Albert Ng and colleagues at Microsoft Research built a touch screen with almost no delay, and found that people dragging on it could notice latencies of only a few milliseconds. <bookmark mark='b'/> Every input travels a pipeline: the sensor, the operating system, the application, rendering, compositing and the display. Each stage that waits for the next frame can add a whole frame, sixteen point seven milliseconds at sixty hertz, the frame budget of Part 42. Latencies add, so each stage must be budgeted.
5ce2d01ee066.zh: 直接操纵的要求，比十分之一秒还要严格。<bookmark mark='a'/>当你在手指下拖动某样东西时，任何延迟都会表现为手指和那样东西之间的一道缝隙。2012年，微软研究院的 Albert Ng 和同事们造了一块几乎没有延迟的触摸屏，发现人们在上面拖动时，能察觉到只有几毫秒的延迟。<bookmark mark='b'/>每一次输入都要走过一条流水线：传感器、操作系统、应用程序、渲染、合成和显示器。每个要等待下一帧的阶段，都可能多出整整一帧，在60赫兹下是16.7毫秒，也就是第42部分的帧预算。延迟会累加，所以每个阶段都必须做预算。

adbc1bae3ee4.en: The second kind of threshold is in size. <bookmark mark='a'/> Two short bars differ by a tenth of a unit, and the difference is easy to see. <bookmark mark='b'/> Add the same tenth to a long bar and it nearly vanishes. <bookmark mark='c'/> To be as visible, the difference must grow with the bar. <bookmark mark='d'/> Ernst Weber found this in the 1830s: the just-noticeable difference is a fixed fraction of the stimulus, a fraction that differs from one sense to another. <bookmark mark='e'/> Gustav Fechner, in 1860, counted those steps, and concluded that sensation grows with the logarithm of the stimulus. It is why loudness is measured in decibels, and, as the next chapter shows, why screens spend more codes on dark tones.
adbc1bae3ee4.zh: 第二类阈值在大小上。<bookmark mark='a'/>两根短条相差十分之一个单位，这个差别很容易看出来。<bookmark mark='b'/>把同样的十分之一加到一根长条上，它几乎就消失了。<bookmark mark='c'/>要同样明显，差别就必须随着条的长度一起增长。<bookmark mark='d'/>韦伯（Ernst Weber）在19世纪30年代发现了这一点：最小可觉差是刺激的一个固定比例，这个比例因感官而异。<bookmark mark='e'/>1860年，费希纳（Gustav Fechner）数了这些台阶，得出结论：感觉随刺激的对数增长。这就是为什么响度用分贝来度量，也是为什么，正如下一章会展示的，屏幕会把更多的编码花在暗色调上。

ad2cde38dc08.en: Some differences need no search at all. <bookmark mark='a'/> One red mark among blue ones is seen at once, however many blue ones there are. <bookmark mark='b'/> So is one tilted line among upright ones. Colour, size, orientation and motion are processed in parallel across the whole field of view, before attention arrives. <bookmark mark='c'/> But find the red tilted line here, among red upright lines and blue tilted ones. Each feature alone is everywhere, and the eye has to check the marks one by one. <bookmark mark='d'/> Anne Treisman and Garry Gelade made this the feature integration theory in 1980. For an interface: mark the one thing that matters with a single feature.
ad2cde38dc08.zh: 有些差别根本不需要搜索。<bookmark mark='a'/>一群蓝色标记里的一个红色标记，一眼就能看到，不管蓝色的有多少个。<bookmark mark='b'/>一群竖直线条里的一条倾斜线条也是这样。颜色、大小、朝向和运动，在注意力到来之前，就已经在整个视野里被并行处理了。<bookmark mark='c'/>但是，请在这里找出那条红色的倾斜线条，它混在红色的竖直线条和蓝色的倾斜线条之中。每种特征单独来看都到处都是，眼睛只好一个一个地检查这些标记。<bookmark mark='d'/>Anne Treisman 和 Garry Gelade 在1980年把这一点发展成了特征整合理论。对界面来说：用单独一种特征，标出那件唯一要紧的东西。

225c27c04b0c.en: <bookmark mark='a'/> Watch these six numbers while the screen flickers. One of them changes each time. In 1997 Ronald Rensink, Kevin O'Regan and James Clark showed that when a brief blank separates two pictures, even large changes go unseen for many seconds. <bookmark mark='b'/> Here, the errors went from seventeen to seventy-one. A page that reloads, or a value that updates during a scroll, is exactly such a blank. <bookmark mark='c'/> So an interface should draw the eye to what changed: animate it, or highlight it briefly.
225c27c04b0c.zh: <bookmark mark='a'/>在屏幕闪烁的时候，盯着这六个数字。每闪一次，其中一个就会变。1997年，Ronald Rensink、Kevin O'Regan 和 James Clark 证明，当两幅画面之间隔着一个短暂的空白时，即使很大的变化，也会在好几秒内不被察觉。<bookmark mark='b'/>在这里，错误从17变成了71。一个重新加载的页面，或者一个在滚动时更新的数值，恰恰就是这样一个空白。<bookmark mark='c'/>所以，界面应该把目光引向变化了的地方：给它加上动画，或者短暂地高亮它。

7f51a0e71dbc.en: Light is a spectrum, energy spread across wavelengths. <bookmark mark='a'/> The eye measures it with three kinds of cone, sensitive to short, medium and long wavelengths. <bookmark mark='b'/> Whatever the spectrum, it is reduced to three responses. <bookmark mark='c'/> Two spectra with the same three responses look identical: metamers, which is why three primaries can imitate most colours we see. <bookmark mark='d'/> In 1931 the CIE fixed a standard observer from colour-matching experiments, the XYZ space. The sRGB standard, from HP and Microsoft in 1996, defines three primaries and a white in XYZ, and almost every screen and web page assumes it.
7f51a0e71dbc.zh: 光是一种光谱，是分布在各个波长上的能量。<bookmark mark='a'/>眼睛用三种视锥细胞来测量它，它们分别对短、中、长波长敏感。<bookmark mark='b'/>无论光谱是什么样子，都被归结为三个响应。<bookmark mark='c'/>两个光谱只要三个响应相同，看起来就一模一样：这叫同色异谱（metamer），也是为什么三种原色就能模仿我们看到的大多数颜色。<bookmark mark='d'/>1931年，CIE 根据配色实验确定了一个标准观察者，也就是 XYZ 空间。sRGB 标准由 HP 和微软在1996年制定，它在 XYZ 中定义了三种原色和一个白点，几乎每块屏幕、每个网页都默认采用它。

9675e9424c0a.en: An sRGB pixel stores code values from 0 to 255, and they are not amounts of light. <bookmark mark='a'/> The transfer curve, close to a power of 2.4, maps code to light. <bookmark mark='b'/> Code 128, the middle of the range, emits only 21.6 percent of white's light. <bookmark mark='c'/> Half of white's light is this much paler grey, b c b c b c. <bookmark mark='d'/> The curve is there because of Weber and Fechner: equal steps of code are roughly equal steps of perceived lightness, so the codes are spent where the eye can tell them apart. The price is that mixing, scaling and lighting must convert to linear light first, a theme of Part 51.
9675e9424c0a.zh: 一个 sRGB 像素存储的是从0到255的编码值，而它们并不是光的量。<bookmark mark='a'/>传递曲线接近2.4次幂，把编码映射成光。<bookmark mark='b'/>编码128，也就是范围的正中间，发出的光只有白色的21.6%。<bookmark mark='c'/>白色一半的光，是这个浅得多的灰色，b c b c b c。<bookmark mark='d'/>这条曲线之所以存在，是因为韦伯和费希纳：编码上相等的步长，大致就是感知明度上相等的步长，所以编码被花在了眼睛能分辨的地方。代价是，混合、缩放和光照都必须先转换到线性光，这是第51部分的一个主题。

5b799f4ce7fc.en: Code values say nothing about how different two colours look. <bookmark mark='a'/> Every colour a screen can show sits in this cube of red, green and blue. <bookmark mark='b'/> Perceptual spaces bend that cube so that distance means difference. CIELAB, from 1976, gives lightness and two opponent axes, green to red and blue to yellow. <bookmark mark='c'/> OKLab, published by Björn Ottosson in 2020, is refitted so that equal distances look more nearly equal and hues stay put as colours lighten. Here is this series' own palette in it, and the cube's red corner. <bookmark mark='d'/> Our conversions pass the checks: white has lightness one hundred in CIELAB and one in OKLab, and sRGB red lands on the published value.
5b799f4ce7fc.zh: 编码值并不能说明两种颜色看起来差多少。<bookmark mark='a'/>屏幕能显示的每一种颜色，都位于这个由红、绿、蓝构成的立方体里。<bookmark mark='b'/>感知空间把这个立方体弯折变形，让距离代表差异。CIELAB 来自1976年，给出明度和两条对立轴：从绿到红，从蓝到黄。<bookmark mark='c'/>OKLab 由 Björn Ottosson 在2020年发表，经过重新拟合，使相等的距离看起来更接近相等，并且颜色变亮时色相保持不变。这里是这个系列自己的调色板在其中的位置，还有立方体的红色顶点。<bookmark mark='d'/>我们的转换通过了检验：白色在 CIELAB 中明度为100，在 OKLab 中为1，sRGB 的红色落在公布的数值上。

cbb8f894f2d4.en: About eight percent of men of European ancestry, and half a percent of women, have a colour-vision deficiency, mostly red and green; those are approximate published figures. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here is this series' palette, as typical vision sees it. <bookmark mark='b'/> Below it, the same six colours simulated for the three kinds of missing cone, with the model of Machado, Oliveira and Fernandes from 2009. <bookmark mark='c'/> For each view, the closest pair in OKLab. <bookmark mark='d'/> The honest finding is about us. Under deuteranopia, the red this series uses for false and the orange it uses for the kernel are only 0.014 apart: nearly the same colour. Red means wrong in these videos, so red can never be the only signal.
cbb8f894f2d4.zh: 在欧洲血统的男性中，大约8%有色觉缺陷，女性中约0.5%，大多是红绿方面的；这些是近似的公开数据。<bookmark mark='a'/>这是这个系列的调色板，在典型视觉下的样子。<bookmark mark='b'/>它下面，是同样六种颜色，针对三种视锥细胞缺失的情况所做的模拟，用的是 Machado、Oliveira 和 Fernandes 2009年的模型。<bookmark mark='c'/>对每一种视觉，找出 OKLab 中最接近的一对颜色。<bookmark mark='d'/>诚实的发现关乎我们自己。在绿色盲（deuteranopia）下，这个系列用来表示“假”的红色，和用来表示内核的橙色，相距只有0.014：几乎是同一种颜色。在这些视频里，红色意味着错误，所以红色永远不能是唯一的信号。

f2cee37801dc.en: Colour also decides whether text can be read. <bookmark mark='a'/> The contrast ratio of the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines compares relative luminances, computed in linear light, each plus a small constant for glare. <bookmark mark='b'/> Every colour in our palette clears 4.5, the level asked for ordinary text, on the dark background; three of them also clear seven. <bookmark mark='c'/> Contrast is not enough, though. A chart that separates two series by red and orange alone <bookmark mark='d'/> becomes one series under deuteranopia. <bookmark mark='e'/> Give each series a shape and a direct label as well, and the chart survives. The lesson: never use colour alone; add shape, position or a label.
f2cee37801dc.zh: 颜色还决定了文字能不能读清楚。<bookmark mark='a'/>《Web 内容无障碍指南》（WCAG）里的对比度，比较的是两个相对亮度，它们在线性光中计算，各自再加上一个代表眩光的小常数。<bookmark mark='b'/>我们调色板里的每种颜色，在深色背景上都超过了4.5，这是普通文字所要求的水平；其中有三种还超过了7。<bookmark mark='c'/>不过，光有对比度还不够。一张只用红色和橙色来区分两个数据系列的图表，<bookmark mark='d'/>在绿色盲下就变成了一个系列。<bookmark mark='e'/>再给每个系列配上一个形状和一个直接标注，这张图表就经受住了考验。教训是：永远不要只用颜色；还要加上形状、位置或标注。

2fa4aeab723e.en: A letter on a screen begins as a shape, not as pixels. <bookmark mark='a'/> A font stores each glyph as an outline: closed paths of Bézier curves, pinned by anchor points on the curve and pulled towards control points off it. <bookmark mark='b'/> TrueType, released by Apple in 1991, uses quadratic curves; PostScript fonts use cubic ones. Either way, one outline serves every size. <bookmark mark='c'/> To draw it, lay the pixel grid over the outline and ask whether each pixel's centre is inside: count how often a ray from the centre crosses the outline, using Part 22's orientation test. An odd count means inside. Part 51 will rasterize triangles the same way.
2fa4aeab723e.zh: 屏幕上的一个字母，起初是一个形状，而不是像素。<bookmark mark='a'/>字体把每个字形存储为一个轮廓：由贝塞尔（Bézier）曲线构成的闭合路径，由曲线上的锚点固定，又被拉向曲线外的控制点。<bookmark mark='b'/>TrueType 由 Apple 在1991年发布，用的是二次曲线；PostScript 字体用的是三次曲线。无论哪种，一个轮廓都适用于所有字号。<bookmark mark='c'/>要画出它，就把像素网格叠在轮廓上，问每个像素的中心是否在里面：从中心发出一条射线，数它穿过轮廓多少次，用的是第22部分的方向测试。奇数次就意味着在里面。第51部分会用同样的方法光栅化三角形。

28aa15588dc3.en: Here is the word Job, drawn by FreeType, the open-source rasterizer, at four sizes. <bookmark mark='a'/> With one bit per pixel, each pixel is on or off. At 8 pixels the whole word gets 23 by 11 of them, and the curves turn into staircases. <bookmark mark='b'/> Antialiasing lets a pixel be partly on: its grey is the share of it the outline covers, so an edge a third of the way across a pixel still shows where it is. <bookmark mark='c'/> The small word uses 41 levels of grey, the large one 111. At eight pixels a stroke is about one pixel wide, and where it lands matters.
28aa15588dc3.zh: 这是单词 Job，由开源光栅化器 FreeType 以四种字号画出来。<bookmark mark='a'/>每个像素只用一位时，像素要么亮，要么灭。在8像素的字号下，整个单词只分到23乘11个像素，曲线变成了阶梯。<bookmark mark='b'/>抗锯齿让一个像素可以部分点亮：它的灰度，就是轮廓覆盖它的比例，所以一条落在像素三分之一处的边缘，依然能显示出它的位置。<bookmark mark='c'/>小号的单词用了41级灰度，大号的用了111级。在8像素时，一笔大约只有一个像素宽，它落在哪里就很要紧了。

ca1d7c8e9eb0.en: Coverage alone does not make small text sharp. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here are three identical stems, like the legs of an m, each one and four tenths of a pixel wide. One becomes a grey smear across two pixels, one is solid on one side, one spreads over three. Equal strokes look unequal. <bookmark mark='b'/> Hinting fixes this. A TrueType font carries small programs, bytecode for a stack machine inside the rasterizer, that move the outline's points onto pixel boundaries at each size, so every stem comes out one crisp pixel wide. <bookmark mark='c'/> It matters most at eight to twelve pixels, where a stroke is a single pixel, and much less on dense screens.
ca1d7c8e9eb0.zh: 仅有覆盖率，并不能让小字变得清晰。<bookmark mark='a'/>这里有三根完全相同的竖笔，就像字母 m 的几条腿，每根宽1.4个像素。一根变成横跨两个像素的灰色污迹，一根一侧是实心的，一根铺开到三个像素上。相等的笔画，看起来并不相等。<bookmark mark='b'/>字体微调（hinting）解决了这个问题。一个 TrueType 字体里带着一些小程序，也就是光栅化器内部一台栈式机器的字节码，它们在每个字号下把轮廓的点移到像素边界上，于是每根竖笔都恰好是清晰的一个像素宽。<bookmark mark='c'/>这在8到12像素时最要紧，那时一笔就只有一个像素；在高密度的屏幕上，就没那么要紧了。

459648bb758d.en: A liquid-crystal pixel is really three stripes: red, green and blue. <bookmark mark='a'/> Treat the pixel as a unit, and a stem starting a third of the way in becomes two dim greys. <bookmark mark='b'/> Light the stripes one by one, and the edge can be placed to a third of a pixel: the horizontal resolution triples. <bookmark mark='c'/> Microsoft shipped this as ClearType in Windows XP, with a filter that spreads each edge across neighbouring stripes to hide the colour fringes. <bookmark mark='d'/> It needs to know the stripe order, so rotating a tablet breaks it; once screens were dense enough, Apple turned it off in macOS, in 2018.
459648bb758d.zh: 液晶屏的一个像素，其实是三条条纹：红、绿、蓝。<bookmark mark='a'/>把像素当作一个整体，一根从三分之一处开始的竖笔，就会变成两个暗淡的灰色。<bookmark mark='b'/>把条纹一条一条地点亮，边缘就能定位到三分之一个像素：水平分辨率变成了三倍。<bookmark mark='c'/>微软在 Windows XP 中以 ClearType 的名字推出了这项技术，并配有一个滤波器，把每条边缘分散到相邻的条纹上，以掩盖彩色的镶边。<bookmark mark='d'/>它需要知道条纹的排列顺序，所以把平板电脑转个方向，它就失效了；等到屏幕足够密，苹果在2018年的 macOS 中把它关掉了。

35b23a1e6335.en: <bookmark mark='a'/> A very long line sends the eye a long way back to the start of the next, and it is easy to land on the wrong one. <bookmark mark='b'/> Robert Bringhurst's Elements of Typographic Style puts a comfortable line at forty-five to seventy-five characters; the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines, at their strictest level, ask for at most eighty, with line spacing of at least one and a half. <bookmark mark='c'/> Fonts of the same size can look very different, because the x-height, the height of the small letters, varies; Verdana and Georgia, made for screens, have large ones. <bookmark mark='d'/> And text needs contrast: Part 42 derived the ratio, and body text needs four and a half to one.
35b23a1e6335.zh: <bookmark mark='a'/>一行太长，眼睛就要走很远，才能回到下一行的开头，而且很容易落到错误的一行上。<bookmark mark='b'/>Robert Bringhurst 的《印刷风格要素》（The Elements of Typographic Style）认为，舒适的一行是45到75个字符；Web 内容无障碍指南（WCAG）在最严格的级别上，要求最多80个字符，行距至少1.5倍。<bookmark mark='c'/>同样字号的字体，看起来可能差别很大，因为 x 字高，也就是小写字母的高度，各不相同；为屏幕设计的 Verdana 和 Georgia，x 字高都很大。<bookmark mark='d'/>文字还需要对比度：第42部分推导出了这个比值，正文需要4.5比1。

17ffcb754e3b.en: Accessibility is design for people whose bodies or minds differ from the designer's. <bookmark mark='a'/> The World Health Organization estimates that about one point three billion people, sixteen per cent of the world, live with a significant disability. <bookmark mark='b'/> And the line is blurry. Microsoft's inclusive design toolkit draws a spectrum: a person with one arm, a person with a broken arm and a parent holding a baby all need a phone that works one-handed. The same goes for blindness, a cataract and a driver's eyes on the road, and for deafness, an ear infection and a noisy bar. <bookmark mark='c'/> Disability is a mismatch between a person and a design, and with age almost everyone meets one.
17ffcb754e3b.zh: 无障碍，是为身体或心智与设计者不同的人所做的设计。<bookmark mark='a'/>世界卫生组织估计，大约13亿人，也就是世界人口的16%，身有严重的残疾。<bookmark mark='b'/>而这条界线是模糊的。微软的包容性设计工具包画出了一个谱系：一个只有一只手臂的人、一个手臂骨折的人，和一个抱着婴儿的家长，都需要一部能单手操作的手机。失明、白内障，和司机盯着路面的眼睛，也是如此；耳聋、耳部感染，和一间嘈杂的酒吧，也是如此。<bookmark mark='c'/>残疾是人与设计之间的不匹配，而随着年龄增长，几乎每个人都会遇到一次。

7ad112e64a3b.en: Each kind of assistive technology asks something different of software. <bookmark mark='a'/> A screen reader speaks the accessibility tree that Part 42 built from the page: this is a button, named Buy. <bookmark mark='b'/> Someone who can press only one or two switches, with a hand, a foot or a breath, steps a highlight through the controls, so every action must be reachable in that order. <bookmark mark='c'/> Magnifiers enlarge the screen; the guidelines ask that text resize to twice its size, and that a page still work at three hundred and twenty pixels wide. <bookmark mark='d'/> Voice control acts on names: say click Buy, and it must find a control whose accessible name contains the visible word.
7ad112e64a3b.zh: 每一类辅助技术，对软件的要求都不一样。<bookmark mark='a'/>屏幕阅读器朗读的，是第42部分从页面构建出的无障碍树：这是一个按钮，名字叫 Buy。<bookmark mark='b'/>有的人只能按一两个开关，用手、用脚，或者用一口气，他们让一个高亮框在各个控件之间逐个移动，所以每个操作都必须能按这个顺序到达。<bookmark mark='c'/>放大器把屏幕放大；指南要求文字能放大到两倍，并且页面在320像素宽时仍然可用。<bookmark mark='d'/>语音控制按名字来操作：说“点击 Buy”，它就必须找到一个控件，其无障碍名称包含那个看得见的词。

108c43486ddb.en: Chapter one's law has an accessibility reading. <bookmark mark='a'/> For a given reach, a wider target is quicker to hit. With chapter one's fit, a sixteen-pixel target four hundred and eighty pixels away takes about 759 milliseconds, a forty-four-pixel one 640. <bookmark mark='b'/> For someone with a tremor, whose hand scatters widely, the difference decides whether the target can be hit at all. WCAG 2.2 sets a minimum of twenty-four by twenty-four CSS pixels, or enough space around a smaller target. <bookmark mark='c'/> And anything done by dragging must also work with a single tap, and everything with a keyboard.
108c43486ddb.zh: 第一章的定律，也可以从无障碍的角度来读。<bookmark mark='a'/>在给定的距离下，目标越宽，就越快点中。用第一章拟合的结果，一个480像素外、16像素宽的目标，大约需要759毫秒，一个44像素宽的目标需要640毫秒。<bookmark mark='b'/>对于手部震颤、落点很分散的人来说，这个差别决定了目标到底能不能点中。WCAG 2.2 规定的最小尺寸是24乘24个 CSS 像素，或者在较小的目标周围留出足够的空间。<bookmark mark='c'/>而且，任何靠拖动完成的操作，也必须能用一次点按完成，所有的操作都必须能用键盘完成。

30694affa8c3.en: Some disabilities affect memory, attention or reading. <bookmark mark='a'/> For them, and for everyone who is tired or in a hurry, the rules are mostly restraint: plain words, short sentences, and navigation that stays the same from page to page, so nothing has to be relearned. <bookmark mark='b'/> A time limit should come with a warning and a way to extend it, or not exist. <bookmark mark='c'/> WCAG 2.2 added that signing in must not depend on remembering or solving a puzzle: let a password manager fill the field, and let people paste. <bookmark mark='d'/> And video needs captions, including the sounds that matter, for deaf viewers, and for everyone watching on a train with the sound off.
30694affa8c3.zh: 有些残疾影响记忆、注意力或阅读。<bookmark mark='a'/>对他们，以及对每一个疲惫或匆忙的人来说，规则主要是克制：浅白的用词，简短的句子，以及在每个页面上都保持不变的导航，这样就不必重新学习任何东西。<bookmark mark='b'/>时间限制应当带有提醒，并提供延长的办法，否则就不该存在。<bookmark mark='c'/>WCAG 2.2 新增规定，登录不能依赖记忆或解谜：要让密码管理器能填写输入框，也要允许人们粘贴。<bookmark mark='d'/>视频还需要字幕，包括那些重要的声音，这既是为了失聪的观众，也是为了每一个在火车上关掉声音观看的人。

29b268f340ab.en: Designing for the edges usually helps the middle. <bookmark mark='a'/> Cuts in the kerb were fought for by wheelchair users; now everyone with a pram, a suitcase or a bicycle uses them, and the pattern is called the curb-cut effect. Captions, made for deaf viewers, are read in every noisy room. <bookmark mark='b'/> The architect Ronald Mace called this universal design: one design for the widest range of people, rather than a special version added later. <bookmark mark='c'/> The web's guidelines rest on four principles. Content must be perceivable, operable, understandable, and robust enough to work with assistive technology. <bookmark mark='d'/> Contrast belongs to the first; Part 42 derived it, and chapter four checked this series' palette.
29b268f340ab.zh: 为边缘人群做的设计，通常也会帮到中间的人。<bookmark mark='a'/>路缘坡道是轮椅使用者争取来的；如今每个推婴儿车、拉行李箱或骑自行车的人都在用它，这种模式被称为路缘坡道效应。字幕是为失聪观众做的，却在每一个嘈杂的房间里被人阅读。<bookmark mark='b'/>建筑师 Ronald Mace 把这称为通用设计：一种设计，面向尽可能广泛的人群，而不是事后再加一个特殊版本。<bookmark mark='c'/>Web 的指南建立在四条原则之上。内容必须可感知、可操作、可理解，并且足够健壮，能与辅助技术配合工作。<bookmark mark='d'/>对比度属于第一条；第42部分推导了它，第四章检查了这个系列的配色。

0e4ac58cb5e2.en: How do you find out what is wrong with a design before your users do? The cheapest way is to inspect it. <bookmark mark='a'/> In 1994 Jakob Nielsen distilled ten rules of thumb from hundreds of usability problems: show people what the system is doing, speak their language, let them undo, be consistent, prevent errors, make choices visible instead of remembered, and so on. <bookmark mark='b'/> In a heuristic evaluation, a few evaluators each check the design against the list on their own, then pool what they found. <bookmark mark='c'/> It is fast and cheap. But it finds the problems experts expect, and real people find others.
0e4ac58cb5e2.zh: 怎样才能赶在用户之前，发现一个设计的毛病？最便宜的办法是检查它。<bookmark mark='a'/>1994年，Jakob Nielsen 从数百个可用性问题中提炼出十条经验法则：让人们看到系统在做什么，说他们的语言，让他们能撤销，保持一致，预防错误，让选项看得见，而不是靠记忆，等等。<bookmark mark='b'/>在启发式评估中，几位评估者各自独立地对照这份清单检查设计，然后汇总他们的发现。<bookmark mark='c'/>它又快又便宜。但它找到的是专家预料到的问题，而真实的人会发现别的问题。

8e873d14b266.en: To find what real people stumble on, watch them. <bookmark mark='a'/> In a think-aloud study a participant is given real tasks, like buying a ticket for a friend, and asked to say what they are thinking as they work. <bookmark mark='b'/> Every hesitation, wrong guess and retreat marks a problem, and the words say why: the person did not know where to say the ticket was for someone else. <bookmark mark='c'/> The facilitator stays quiet, and never helps. Clayton Lewis brought the method into interface design at IBM in 1982, from the psychology of verbal reports. The rule is to watch what people do, and not to ask what they would do.
8e873d14b266.zh: 要找到真实的人会在哪里绊倒，就去观察他们。<bookmark mark='a'/>在出声思维研究中，参与者拿到真实的任务，比如给朋友买一张票，并被要求一边做，一边说出自己在想什么。<bookmark mark='b'/>每一次犹豫、每一个错误的猜测、每一次退回，都标出一个问题，而他们说的话解释了原因：这个人不知道该在哪里说明，这张票是给别人的。<bookmark mark='c'/>主持人保持安静，从不帮忙。Clayton Lewis 在1982年，把这种方法从言语报告的心理学引入了 IBM 的界面设计。规则是：观察人们做什么，而不是问他们会做什么。

a99770b45b60.en: How many participants are enough? Jakob Nielsen and Thomas Landauer answered with a model in 1993. <bookmark mark='a'/> Suppose each user, independently, runs into each problem with the same probability L. Averaged over the projects they studied, L was about 0.31. <bookmark mark='b'/> One user misses a given problem with probability one minus L. All n users miss it with probability one minus L to the power n, because independent chances multiply, as in Part 2. <bookmark mark='c'/> So the share of problems found is one minus that. <bookmark mark='d'/> One user finds 31 per cent, two find 52, three 67, four 77, and five 84: the famous claim that five users find most of the problems.
a99770b45b60.zh: 需要多少名参与者才够？Jakob Nielsen 和 Thomas Landauer 在1993年用一个模型给出了回答。<bookmark mark='a'/>假设每个用户独立地以同样的概率 L 遇到每一个问题。在他们研究的那些项目上取平均，L 约为0.31。<bookmark mark='b'/>一个用户错过某个问题的概率，是1减 L。n 个用户全都错过它的概率，是1减 L 的 n 次方，因为相互独立的概率相乘，就像第2部分那样。<bookmark mark='c'/>所以，被发现的问题所占的比例，是1减去这个值。<bookmark mark='d'/>一个用户能发现31%，两个发现52%，三个67%，四个77%，五个84%：这就是那个著名的说法，五个用户就能发现大部分问题。

8f5e738cab39.en: The model assumed every problem is equally easy to find. Real ones are not. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here is the curve when each problem is found with the same probability. <bookmark mark='b'/> Now let visibility vary: a few problems hit almost everyone, many hit only a few. We drew each problem's probability from a Beta distribution with the same average, point three one. With five users the share found falls from 84 to 71 per cent. <bookmark mark='c'/> To find 84 per cent now takes 11 users, because the problems few people hit are the ones that take longest to see, and the average hides them.
8f5e738cab39.zh: 这个模型假设每个问题都同样容易被发现。真实的问题并非如此。<bookmark mark='a'/>这是每个问题都以相同概率被发现时的曲线。<bookmark mark='b'/>现在让可见度变化：少数问题几乎人人都会碰到，许多问题只有少数人碰到。我们从一个平均值同样是0.31的 Beta 分布中，抽取每个问题的概率。在五个用户时，被发现的比例从84%降到了71%。<bookmark mark='c'/>现在要发现84%，需要11个用户，因为很少有人碰到的那些问题，恰恰是最久才会被看见的，而平均值把它们掩盖了。

31d381ab2b86.en: So the five-user rule needs care. <bookmark mark='a'/> L is an average over projects, and it varies with the product, the task and the people. <bookmark mark='b'/> A problem that only one user in twenty hits is found by five users less than a quarter of the time, however severe it is, which is why rare but costly failures need other methods too: logs, support calls, and the experiments of the next chapter. <bookmark mark='c'/> What the curve does support is iteration. One round of fifteen users would find nearly everything in today's design, but most of it is found by the first five; fix that, and the next five find the problems the old ones were hiding. Nielsen's own advice was three rounds of five.
31d381ab2b86.zh: 所以，五用户法则需要谨慎对待。<bookmark mark='a'/>L 是对许多项目取的平均，它随产品、任务和人群而变化。<bookmark mark='b'/>一个二十个用户里只有一个会碰到的问题，五个用户能发现它的概率不到四分之一，无论它有多严重；这就是为什么罕见但代价高昂的故障，还需要别的方法：日志、客服电话，以及下一章的实验。<bookmark mark='c'/>这条曲线真正支持的，是迭代。一轮15个用户几乎能找出今天这个设计中的所有问题，但其中大部分是前5个用户找到的；把这些修好，接下来的5个用户就会发现那些被旧问题掩盖住的问题。Nielsen 自己的建议是三轮，每轮五人。

07476104a125.en: Where intuition runs out, run an experiment. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each arriving user is assigned by a coin: heads, the current page; tails, the new one. <bookmark mark='b'/> Because a coin decides and not a person, the two groups differ only by chance, in every trait, even ones nobody measured, such as how many are returning customers. <bookmark mark='c'/> With large groups, Part 20's concentration makes their averages nearly equal. So if the groups then behave differently, the cause is the change, or chance. This is Ronald Fisher's randomized experiment, and a statistical test measures the chance.
07476104a125.zh: 直觉用尽的地方，就做实验。<bookmark mark='a'/>每个到来的用户，都由抛硬币来分配：正面，看现在的页面；反面，看新的页面。<bookmark mark='b'/>因为做决定的是硬币，而不是人，两组之间只有偶然的差别，在每一项特征上都是如此，甚至包括没人测量过的特征，比如其中有多少是回头客。<bookmark mark='c'/>组足够大时，第20部分讲的集中现象，会让它们的平均值几乎相等。所以，如果两组之后的表现不同，原因要么是这项改动，要么是偶然。这就是罗纳德·费希尔（Ronald Fisher）的随机化实验，而统计检验衡量的，正是这个偶然。

a2a878ac00a6.en: Here is the standard test. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each arm converts a share of its users, and the observed difference is B's rate minus A's. <bookmark mark='b'/> Suppose the change did nothing: then both arms share one rate, estimated by pooling them. <bookmark mark='c'/> A rate's variance is p times one minus p over n, and the two arms' variances add. <bookmark mark='d'/> Divide the difference by the resulting standard error. For large samples z is nearly standard normal, and the p-value is the chance of a z this far from zero if nothing changed. <bookmark mark='e'/> Five hundred conversions against five hundred and sixty, out of ten thousand each, is a twelve per cent lift, yet z is only 1.89 and the p-value 0.058: not significant at five per cent.
a2a878ac00a6.zh: 这是标准的检验。<bookmark mark='a'/>每一组都有一部分用户发生转化，观察到的差异，是 B 的转化率减去 A 的转化率。<bookmark mark='b'/>假设这项改动毫无作用：那么两组共享同一个转化率，把两组合并起来就能估计它。<bookmark mark='c'/>一个比率的方差，是 p 乘以1减 p，再除以 n，而两组的方差相加。<bookmark mark='d'/>用差异除以由此得到的标准误。样本很大时，z 近似服从标准正态分布，而 p 值就是在什么都没变的情况下，z 离零这么远的概率。<bookmark mark='e'/>各一万名用户中，500次转化对560次，是12%的提升，但 z 只有1.89，p 值是0.058：在5%的水平上并不显著。

400dfee730fc.en: A test can be wrong in two ways. <bookmark mark='a'/> If the change did nothing, the estimated difference scatters around zero, with a spread of one standard error. We declare a winner beyond one point nine six of them, so we are fooled five per cent of the time: that is alpha. <bookmark mark='b'/> If the change really helps by delta, the estimate scatters around delta instead, and whenever it falls short of the line we miss a real effect: that is beta, and one minus beta is the power. <bookmark mark='c'/> For eighty per cent power, delta must sit nought point eight four standard errors beyond the line.
400dfee730fc.zh: 检验可能以两种方式出错。<bookmark mark='a'/>如果改动毫无作用，估计出的差异会围绕零散布，散布的幅度是一个标准误。我们在超过1.96个标准误时宣布胜者，所以有5%的时候会被骗：这就是 alpha。<bookmark mark='b'/>如果改动确实带来了 delta 的提升，估计值就会围绕 delta 散布，而每当它没能越过那条线，我们就错过了一个真实的效应：这就是 beta，而1减 beta 就是功效。<bookmark mark='c'/>要有80%的功效，delta 必须位于那条线之外0.84个标准误处。

884a91cca3e9.en: That picture is a recipe for the sample size. <bookmark mark='a'/> Delta must be one point nine six plus nought point eight four standard errors, and the standard error is sigma times the root of two over n. <bookmark mark='b'/> Solve for n. <bookmark mark='c'/> The constant comes to fifteen point seven, so n is about sixteen sigma squared over delta squared: every experimenter's rule of thumb. <bookmark mark='d'/> On a five per cent conversion rate, a five per cent relative lift needs about 119 thousand users in each arm; the rule says 121.6 thousand. Halve the lift and you need four times as many: a one per cent lift needs about 3 million per arm.
884a91cca3e9.zh: 这张图，就是计算样本量的配方。<bookmark mark='a'/>delta 必须等于1.96加0.84个标准误，而标准误是 sigma 乘以 n 分之2的平方根。<bookmark mark='b'/>解出 n。<bookmark mark='c'/>常数算出来是15.7，所以 n 约为16乘 sigma 的平方，除以 delta 的平方：这是每个做实验的人都熟悉的经验法则。<bookmark mark='d'/>在5%的转化率上，5%的相对提升，每组大约需要119千名用户；经验法则给出的是121.6千名。提升减半，所需人数就变成四倍：1%的提升，每组大约需要3百万名用户。

ec6d9f3e4578.en: Formulas built on approximations deserve a check. <bookmark mark='a'/> We simulated two thousand experiments with a true five per cent lift and 119,302 users per arm. <bookmark mark='b'/> The test found the lift in 78.9 per cent of them, the eighty per cent we designed for, to within the simulation's noise. <bookmark mark='c'/> With half the users, the standard error grows by the square root of two, and delta now sits barely past the line. Power falls to 50 per cent: a real improvement missed half the time. <bookmark mark='d'/> Worse, when such a test does come out significant, it overstates the effect, because only the lucky overestimates cross the line.
ec6d9f3e4578.zh: 建立在近似之上的公式，值得核对一下。<bookmark mark='a'/>我们模拟了两千次实验，真实提升为5%，每组119302名用户。<bookmark mark='b'/>检验在其中78.9%的实验里发现了这个提升，正是我们设计的80%，误差在模拟的噪声之内。<bookmark mark='c'/>用户减半，标准误就增大到根号2倍，delta 现在只是勉强越过那条线。功效降到50%：一个真实的改进，有一半的时候被错过了。<bookmark mark='d'/>更糟的是，当这样的检验真的得出显著结果时，它会夸大效应，因为只有那些幸运的高估，才能越过那条线。

26d09bb55cbc.en: Here is an experiment with nothing in it: two identical versions, an A/A test, with a thousand users a day in each and a conversion rate of five percent. <bookmark mark='a'/> Every morning someone runs last chapter's z-test on everything so far. <bookmark mark='b'/> With no difference, the p-value has nowhere to settle. On any one day it is equally likely to be anywhere between zero and one, and from day to day it wanders, <bookmark mark='c'/> sometimes close to the red line. Of these six, one falls below it, on the last morning. Look often enough, and any of them might.
26d09bb55cbc.zh: 这里有一个什么都没有的实验：两个完全相同的版本，也就是一次 A/A 测试，每组每天一千名用户，转化率为5%。<bookmark mark='a'/>每天早上，都有人对到目前为止的全部数据，运行上一章的 z 检验。<bookmark mark='b'/>既然没有差异，p 值就无处落定。在任何一天，它落在0到1之间任何位置的可能性都相同，而且它一天天地游走，<bookmark mark='c'/>有时离红线很近。这六个实验中，有一个跌到了红线以下，就在最后一个早上。看的次数足够多，它们中的任何一个都可能这样。

e21a25824348.en: Now simulate four thousand of them, and stop each one the first morning its p-value falls below five percent, declaring a winner. <bookmark mark='a'/> On the first day, 5 percent stop, as promised. After a week, 17 percent have stopped. After two weeks, 23. <bookmark mark='b'/> By day thirty, 28 percent of experiments with no effect at all have announced one. <bookmark mark='c'/> The same experiments, looked at only once, at the end, give 4 percent. The test was never wrong; the stopping rule was. Five percent is a promise about one look, not thirty.
e21a25824348.zh: 现在模拟四千个这样的实验，每个实验在它的 p 值第一次跌破5%的那个早上就停下来，宣布胜者。<bookmark mark='a'/>第一天，有5%停下，和承诺的一样。一周之后，17%已经停下。两周之后，23%。<bookmark mark='b'/>到第三十天，在根本没有效应的实验中，有28%宣布了一个效应。<bookmark mark='c'/>同样这些实验，如果只在最后看一次，结果是4%。检验从来没有错；错的是停止规则。5%是对一次查看的承诺，而不是对三十次。

d05141627ad2.en: Why does looking hurt? <bookmark mark='a'/> Turn each p-value back into its z-statistic. The test rejects when z rises above one point nine six. <bookmark mark='b'/> With no real difference, z is a random walk divided by the square root of its length: Part 20's concentration, in motion. <bookmark mark='c'/> The law of the iterated logarithm, proved by Aleksandr Khinchin in 1924, says its peaks keep returning to about the square root of two log log n, which grows without limit. <bookmark mark='d'/> So a walk watched forever crosses any fixed line. Thirty separate tests would give 79 percent false positives; daily looks share most of their data, so we saw 28, but every look adds some.
d05141627ad2.zh: 为什么多看会有害？<bookmark mark='a'/>把每个 p 值变回它的 z 统计量。当 z 超过1.96时，检验就拒绝。<bookmark mark='b'/>没有真实差异时，z 是一个随机游走除以其长度的平方根：这是第20部分的集中现象，动了起来。<bookmark mark='c'/>重对数律由亚历山大·辛钦（Aleksandr Khinchin）在1924年证明，它说 z 的峰值会不断回到大约根号下2 log log n 的高度，而这个值会无限增长。<bookmark mark='d'/>所以一个被永远盯着的游走，会越过任何一条固定的线。三十次相互独立的检验，会给出79%的假阳性；每天的查看共享了大部分数据，所以我们看到的是28%，但每多看一次，都会增加一些。

27e1fe5f7d35.en: The fix is a test built to be watched. <bookmark mark='a'/> Abraham Wald's sequential test compared the likelihood of the data under an effect with its likelihood under none; Herbert Robbins, in 1970, averaged that ratio over a range of plausible effects. <bookmark mark='b'/> Stop when it reaches one over alpha, twenty. <bookmark mark='c'/> With no effect, the ratio is a fair bet: its expected value stays one however long you play, and Ville's inequality says it ever reaches twenty with probability at most one in twenty. <bookmark mark='d'/> In z units the boundary is no longer flat: it starts high and comes down slowly. <bookmark mark='e'/> Ramesh Johari, Pete Koomen, Leonid Pekelis and David Walsh turned this into always-valid p-values, safe to check every morning.
27e1fe5f7d35.zh: 解决办法，是一种专门为被盯着看而构建的检验。<bookmark mark='a'/>亚伯拉罕·瓦尔德（Abraham Wald）的序贯检验，比较的是数据在有效应时的似然，与在无效应时的似然；Herbert Robbins 在1970年，把这个比值在一系列合理的效应上取了平均。<bookmark mark='b'/>当它达到 alpha 分之一，也就是20时，就停下。<bookmark mark='c'/>没有效应时，这个比值是一场公平的赌局：无论玩多久，它的期望值都保持为1，而 Ville 不等式说，它曾经达到20的概率至多是二十分之一。<bookmark mark='d'/>换成 z 的单位，边界就不再是平的：它起点很高，然后缓慢下降。<bookmark mark='e'/>Ramesh Johari、Pete Koomen、Leonid Pekelis 和 David Walsh 把这变成了始终有效的 p 值，每天早上查看都是安全的。

d1d9b90dccd2.en: We ran the mixture test on the same traffic, checked daily. <bookmark mark='a'/> Daily z-tests had 28 percent false positives. <bookmark mark='b'/> The mixture test, its spread tuned to five percent lifts, had 0.4 percent; tuned to ten percent lifts, 1.2. Both under five. <bookmark mark='c'/> Now give the new version a real ten percent lift. Within thirty days the first catches it 39 percent of the time, at a median of day 22, and the second 51 percent, by day 18. <bookmark mark='d'/> A fixed test with eighty percent power needs almost thirty thousand users per arm: the whole month, and one look. That is the trade: valid at every look, paid for in power.
d1d9b90dccd2.zh: 我们在同样的流量上运行了混合检验，每天查看一次。<bookmark mark='a'/>每天做 z 检验，有28%的假阳性。<bookmark mark='b'/>混合检验的散布按5%的提升来调时，假阳性是0.4%；按10%的提升来调时，是1.2%。两者都低于5%。<bookmark mark='c'/>现在给新版本一个真实的10%提升。在三十天内，第一个检验有39%的时候能抓住它，中位数在第22天；第二个是51%，在第18天。<bookmark mark='d'/>一个功效为80%的固定样本检验，每组需要将近三万名用户：整整一个月，只看一次。这就是其中的权衡：每次查看都有效，代价是功效。

f0ed4bc89426.en: Chapter ten. Less noise, same truth.
f0ed4bc89426.zh: 第十章：更少的噪声，同样的真相。

ba9819f67a73.en: Most of the variation in a metric has nothing to do with the experiment. A user who spent a lot last month will probably spend a lot this month, whatever version they see. <bookmark mark='a'/> Plot each user's metric during the experiment against the same metric in the month before. The spread of the metric is mostly who the user is. <bookmark mark='b'/> In 2013 Alex Deng, Ya Xu, Ron Kohavi and Toby Walker, at Microsoft, called the remedy CUPED. <bookmark mark='c'/> Subtract from each user what their past predicts: theta times their pre-period metric, less its average. <bookmark mark='d'/> The cloud flattens, and the spread shrinks. The difference between the versions is untouched.
ba9819f67a73.zh: 一个指标中的大部分变化，都与实验无关。一个上个月花了很多钱的用户，这个月很可能也会花很多，不管他看到的是哪个版本。<bookmark mark='a'/>把每个用户在实验期间的指标，与他在前一个月的同一指标画在一起。指标的散布，主要取决于这个用户是谁。<bookmark mark='b'/>2013年，微软的 Alex Deng、Ya Xu、Ron Kohavi 和 Toby Walker，把这个补救办法称为 CUPED。<bookmark mark='c'/>从每个用户身上，减去他的过去所预测的部分：theta 乘以他实验前那段时间的指标与其平均值之差。<bookmark mark='d'/>点云变平了，散布缩小了。而两个版本之间的差异，丝毫没有改变。

783dc2b8d873.en: How much does it help? <bookmark mark='a'/> Expand the variance of the adjusted metric: the variance of Y, minus twice theta times the covariance, plus theta squared times the variance of X. <bookmark mark='b'/> It is a parabola in theta, smallest where the derivative vanishes: at the covariance over the variance of X, the slope of the regression line. <bookmark mark='c'/> Put that back, and the variance is the plain one times one minus rho squared, rho being the correlation of past and present. <bookmark mark='d'/> And the truth is the same, because X was measured before randomization: both groups have the same average past, in expectation, so the adjustment removes noise and not effect. Hence the one rule: never adjust by anything the treatment could change.
783dc2b8d873.zh: 它能帮多大的忙？<bookmark mark='a'/>把调整后指标的方差展开：Y 的方差，减去2倍 theta 乘以协方差，再加上 theta 的平方乘以 X 的方差。<bookmark mark='b'/>这是关于 theta 的一条抛物线，在导数为零的地方最小：也就是协方差除以 X 的方差，即回归直线的斜率。<bookmark mark='c'/>把它代回去，方差就等于原来的方差，乘以1减 rho 的平方，rho 是过去与现在的相关系数。<bookmark mark='d'/>而真相保持不变，因为 X 是在随机化之前测量的：从期望上看，两组过去的平均值相同，所以这项调整去掉的是噪声，而不是效应。由此只有一条规则：永远不要用任何可能被实验处理改变的东西来做调整。

b535f3ba3869.en: We checked the formula on simulated experiments: twenty thousand users per arm, repeated two thousand times for each of five correlations. <bookmark mark='a'/> The blue bars are the measured variance with CUPED, divided by the variance without; the yellow marks are one minus rho squared. <bookmark mark='b'/> They agree, from no help at all when the past says nothing, <bookmark mark='c'/> to a variance cut to 0.50 at a correlation of point seven, and 0.19 at point nine. <bookmark mark='d'/> Variance falls as one over the number of users, so a correlation of point seven is worth about 2 times the traffic, and point nine about 5 times: weeks of experiment, for one line of arithmetic.
b535f3ba3869.zh: 我们在模拟实验上检验了这个公式：每组两万名用户，五种相关系数，每种重复两千次。<bookmark mark='a'/>蓝色的柱是用了 CUPED 之后测得的方差，除以不用时的方差；黄色的标记是 1 减 ρ 的平方。<bookmark mark='b'/>两者吻合：从过去什么也说明不了时的毫无帮助，<bookmark mark='c'/>到相关系数为 0.7 时方差降到 0.50，0.9 时降到 0.19。<bookmark mark='d'/>方差按用户数的倒数下降，所以 0.7 的相关系数大约相当于 2 倍的流量，0.9 大约相当于 5 倍：几周的实验，换成一行算术。

9fad307587d9.en: Here is what that means for one experiment's conclusion. <bookmark mark='a'/> The true effect is point zero two standard deviations. Without CUPED, the ninety-five percent interval reaches almost as far as the effect itself on either side, and only just clears zero. <bookmark mark='b'/> Now raise the correlation with the past. At point five the interval narrows a little; <bookmark mark='c'/> at point seven, by 29 percent; <bookmark mark='d'/> at point nine, by 56 percent, to less than half its width. <bookmark mark='e'/> The same users and the same effect; the only thing removed is the noise that each user's own history already explained.
9fad307587d9.zh: 来看看这对一次实验的结论意味着什么。<bookmark mark='a'/>真实的效应是 0.02 个标准差。不用 CUPED，95% 置信区间向两侧伸出的距离，几乎和效应本身一样大，只是勉强避开了零。<bookmark mark='b'/>现在提高与过去的相关性。在 0.5 时，区间窄了一点；<bookmark mark='c'/>在 0.7 时，窄了 29%；<bookmark mark='d'/>在 0.9 时，窄了 56%，不到原来宽度的一半。<bookmark mark='e'/>同样的用户，同样的效应；去掉的只是每个用户自己的历史早已解释了的那部分噪声。

ebde607f8dc9.en: CUPED belongs to an old family. <bookmark mark='a'/> When users fall into groups that behave differently, light and heavy users say, part of the spread lies between the groups. <bookmark mark='b'/> Stratification compares the versions within each group and then weights the groups, so the between-group part drops out of the noise. <bookmark mark='c'/> In general, regress the metric on the treatment and on covariates measured before it; the treatment's coefficient is the effect. CUPED is the one-covariate case, and the covariate can be a model's prediction from the past. <bookmark mark='d'/> Winston Lin showed in 2013 that, with interaction terms, this cannot hurt precision in large samples.
ebde607f8dc9.zh: CUPED 属于一个古老的家族。<bookmark mark='a'/>当用户分成行为不同的几组，比如轻度用户和重度用户，波动的一部分就落在组与组之间。<bookmark mark='b'/>分层法在每一组内部比较两个版本，再给各组加权，于是组间的那部分就从噪声里消失了。<bookmark mark='c'/>一般地，把指标对处理、以及处理之前测得的协变量做回归；处理的系数就是效应。CUPED 是只有一个协变量的情形，而这个协变量可以是一个模型根据过去做出的预测。<bookmark mark='d'/>Winston Lin 在 2013 年证明，加上交互项以后，这样做在大样本下不会损害精度。

4db1f58c19a3.zh: 第十一章：大规模下的陷阱。

094b9991c755.en: Experiments report dozens of metrics. Take twenty, and a change that moved none of them. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each has a five percent chance of looking significant. <bookmark mark='b'/> Run the experiment, and one metric lights up; run another, and a different one does. <bookmark mark='c'/> The chance that at least one lights up is one minus point nine five to the twentieth, 64 percent; our simulation found 64. <bookmark mark='d'/> Report the metric that moved, and you have usually reported noise: Part 2's counting, turned against us.
094b9991c755.zh: 实验会报告几十个指标。取二十个，再取一个哪个指标都没有改变的改动。<bookmark mark='a'/>每个指标都有 5% 的机会看起来显著。<bookmark mark='b'/>跑一次实验，有一个指标亮了；再跑一次，亮的是另一个。<bookmark mark='c'/>至少有一个亮起来的概率，是 1 减去 0.95 的 20 次方，即 64%；我们的模拟得到的是 64%。<bookmark mark='d'/>报告那个动了的指标，你报告的通常就是噪声：这是第2部分的计数，掉转过来对准了我们自己。

e99ff9d8aa79.en: The cure is to be less impressed the more you look. <bookmark mark='a'/> Bonferroni divides the threshold by the number of tests: safe, but strict. <bookmark mark='b'/> In 1995 Yoav Benjamini and Yosef Hochberg proposed a gentler line: sort the p-values, and compare the i-th smallest with alpha times i over k. <bookmark mark='c'/> Everything up to the last point under the line is a discovery. <bookmark mark='d'/> This controls the false discovery rate, the expected share of discoveries that are false. With nothing real, only 5 percent of our experiments made any.
e99ff9d8aa79.zh: 解药是：看得越多，就越不要轻易被打动。<bookmark mark='a'/>Bonferroni 校正把阈值除以检验的次数：安全，但严格。<bookmark mark='b'/>1995年，Yoav Benjamini 和 Yosef Hochberg 提出了一条更温和的线：把 p 值排好序，把第 i 小的那个与 α 乘以 i 除以 k 相比较。<bookmark mark='c'/>直到最后一个落在线下的点为止，所有的点都算作发现。<bookmark mark='d'/>这控制的是错误发现率，也就是发现之中错误发现所占比例的期望。在什么都不是真的情况下，我们的实验里只有 5% 做出了任何发现。

61ef0c5267fa.en: Before reading any metric, check the split. <bookmark mark='a'/> A fifty-fifty test that ends with 50,000 users in one arm and 49,000 in the other looks close. <bookmark mark='b'/> Pearson's chi-squared test disagrees: chi-squared is 10.1, and a gap this large happens by chance about 15 times in ten thousand. <bookmark mark='c'/> 50,100 against 49,900 is ordinary luck. <bookmark mark='d'/> A mismatch means something removed users unevenly: a redirect, a bot filter, a crash that stops one version logging. The users who remain are no longer comparable, so every metric is suspect.
61ef0c5267fa.zh: 读任何指标之前，先检查分组。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个五五开的测试，结束时一组有 50000 名用户，另一组有 49000 名，看上去很接近。<bookmark mark='b'/>皮尔逊（Pearson）卡方检验不同意：卡方值是 10.1，这么大的差距靠运气出现，大约是一万次里 15 次。<bookmark mark='c'/>50100 对 49900，则只是寻常的运气。<bookmark mark='d'/>不匹配意味着有什么东西不均匀地去掉了用户：一次重定向，一个机器人过滤器，一次让某个版本停止记录日志的崩溃。剩下的用户不再可比，所以每个指标都值得怀疑。

97da974d036b.en: Averages can reverse. <bookmark mark='a'/> A redesign converts better on desktop, 11.2 percent against 10, <bookmark mark='b'/> and better on mobile, 5.8 against 3. <bookmark mark='c'/> Yet overall it converts worse: 6.5 percent against 7.7. <bookmark mark='d'/> Its visitors were mostly on mobile, where everyone converts less, and the overall rate weights segments by traffic: Simpson's paradox, after Edward Simpson's paper of 1951. <bookmark mark='e'/> A randomized test gives both arms the same mix, so a mix like this is itself a warning: the split changed midway, or nothing was randomized.
97da974d036b.zh: 平均值可能会反转。<bookmark mark='a'/>一次改版在桌面端转化得更好，11.2% 对 10%，<bookmark mark='b'/>在移动端也更好，5.8 对 3。<bookmark mark='c'/>可是总体上它转化得更差：6.5% 对 7.7%。<bookmark mark='d'/>它的访客大多在移动端，而在那里谁的转化率都更低；总体转化率又是按流量给各个细分加权的：这就是辛普森悖论，得名于 Edward Simpson 1951年的论文。<bookmark mark='e'/>随机化测试让两组有同样的构成，所以出现这样的构成本身就是一个警告：分组中途变了，或者根本没有随机化。

f7ba36aea3c9.en: A two-week test measures two weeks of behaviour. <bookmark mark='a'/> A new button gets clicked because it is new: the novelty effect, a lift that fades. <bookmark mark='b'/> The opposite is primacy: people used to the old design stumble at first. <bookmark mark='c'/> So plot the effect against days since each user first saw the change, look at new users, who have no habits, and run until the curve flattens. <bookmark mark='d'/> And when users affect each other, as buyers in a marketplace do, the test itself is biased; that is for the frontier chapter.
f7ba36aea3c9.zh: 一个为期两周的测试，测到的是两周的行为。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个新按钮被点击，是因为它新：这就是新奇效应，一种会消退的提升。<bookmark mark='b'/>与之相反的是首因效应：习惯了旧设计的人，一开始会磕磕绊绊。<bookmark mark='c'/>所以，要把效应画成用户第一次看到改动以来的天数的函数，看看还没有养成习惯的新用户，并且一直跑到曲线变平为止。<bookmark mark='d'/>而当用户彼此影响时，比如市场里的买家，测试本身就是有偏的；这一点留给前沿一章。

16d80692339a.en: The last pitfall is wanting to believe. <bookmark mark='a'/> Twyman's law, named after the British audience researcher Tony Twyman and made a rule of experimentation by Ron Kohavi: any figure that looks interesting or different is usually wrong. <bookmark mark='b'/> A test reports revenue up thirty-eight percent. <bookmark mark='c'/> Before celebrating, check the split, check whether logging changed, look for bots or one enormous customer, and run an A/A test through the same pipeline. <bookmark mark='d'/> Real improvements are usually small. A huge one is usually a bug.
16d80692339a.zh: 最后一个陷阱，是想要相信。<bookmark mark='a'/>Twyman 定律，以英国受众研究者 Tony Twyman 命名，由 Ron Kohavi 定为实验的一条规则：任何看起来有趣或与众不同的数字，通常都是错的。<bookmark mark='b'/>一个测试报告收入上涨了 38%。<bookmark mark='c'/>庆祝之前，先检查分组，检查日志记录是否变了，找找有没有机器人或者某一个极大的客户，再让一次 A/A 测试走同一条流水线。<bookmark mark='d'/>真正的改进通常很小。巨大的改进，通常是一个 bug。

d1f974acb773.zh: 第十二章：老虎机与指标。

cf8beaa8e2cf.en: An A/B test gives the worse version half its traffic until the end, on purpose. A bandit, named after the casino's one-armed bandits, shifts traffic while it learns. <bookmark mark='a'/> Part 26 of AI, Built met the oldest good rule, Thompson sampling, from William Thompson in 1933. Keep a belief about each version's conversion rate. <bookmark mark='b'/> For each visitor, draw one plausible rate from each belief, and show the version whose draw is higher. <bookmark mark='c'/> As evidence arrives the beliefs narrow, and a version is tried exactly as often as it might still be the best.
cf8beaa8e2cf.zh: A/B 测试有意让较差的版本一直拿到一半的流量，直到结束。老虎机算法（bandit），得名于赌场里被称作“独臂强盗”的老虎机，会一边学习，一边转移流量。<bookmark mark='a'/>《人工智能，从零搭建》第26部分见过其中最古老的好规则：汤普森采样，来自 1933年的 William Thompson。为每个版本的转化率保持一个信念。<bookmark mark='b'/>对每个访客，从每个信念中抽出一个可信的转化率，然后展示抽到的值更高的那个版本。<bookmark mark='c'/>随着证据到来，信念会变窄，而一个版本被尝试的频率，恰好等于它仍然可能是最好那个的概率。

34c09ddc1d2e.en: We raced the two on 100,000 visitors, with versions converting 5 and 5.5 percent. <bookmark mark='a'/> The fifty-fifty split loses about 253 conversions against always showing the better one: its regret. Thompson sampling loses about 48. <bookmark mark='b'/> But look at what each learns. The split measures the difference with a standard deviation of 0.14 points. The bandit, having starved the worse version, is about 5 times less precise, and its interval easily includes zero. <bookmark mark='c'/> So: bandits for optimizing, when only the reward matters, like a headline that lives a day; A/B tests for learning how big an effect is.
34c09ddc1d2e.zh: 我们让两者在 100000 名访客上比赛，两个版本的转化率分别是 5% 和 5.5%。<bookmark mark='a'/>与始终展示更好的那个相比，五五分组大约损失 253 次转化：这是它的遗憾。汤普森采样大约损失 48 次。<bookmark mark='b'/>但看看各自学到了什么。分组测出的差异，标准差是 0.14 个百分点。老虎机算法让较差的版本饿着，精度大约差了 5 倍，它的区间很容易就包含零。<bookmark mark='c'/>所以：要优化、只在乎回报的时候，用老虎机算法，比如一个只活一天的标题；要弄清一个效应有多大，用 A/B 测试。

41d8a68a6982.en: An experiment must know what better means. <bookmark mark='a'/> Companies choose a north-star metric, the one number that stands for value delivered to users, here weekly active buyers. <bookmark mark='b'/> Under it sit driver metrics that move faster and that a team can actually change. <bookmark mark='c'/> Beside them are guardrails: load time, crashes, unsubscribes, support tickets, which must not get worse whatever else improves. <bookmark mark='d'/> A change ships when the overall evaluation criterion, as Ron Kohavi calls it, improves and no guardrail regresses.
41d8a68a6982.zh: 一个实验必须知道“更好”是什么意思。<bookmark mark='a'/>公司会选定一个北极星指标：一个代表为用户交付的价值的数字，这里是每周活跃买家数。<bookmark mark='b'/>它下面是驱动指标，变化更快，而且团队真的能改变它们。<bookmark mark='c'/>它们旁边是护栏指标：加载时间、崩溃、退订、客服工单，无论别的方面改善了多少，这些都不能变差。<bookmark mark='d'/>当 Ron Kohavi 所说的总体评价标准有所改善，而且没有任何护栏指标退步时，一个改动才会上线。

3e0ab05bb2cc.en: Any metric can be gamed by the experiments meant to improve it. <bookmark mark='a'/> The economist Charles Goodhart observed it of monetary targets in 1975; the anthropologist Marilyn Strathern gave it the famous wording: when a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure. <bookmark mark='b'/> Push hard on clicks and clickbait wins; the metric keeps rising after what it stood for starts to fall. <bookmark mark='c'/> A learning system finds that gap faster than any person: reward hacking, from Part 31 of AI, Built. <bookmark mark='d'/> The defences: several metrics, guardrails, long holdouts, and asking users.
3e0ab05bb2cc.zh: 任何指标，都可能被本该改善它的实验钻空子。<bookmark mark='a'/>经济学家古德哈特（Charles Goodhart）在 1975年就货币目标指出了这一点；人类学家 Marilyn Strathern 给了它那句著名的表述：当一个度量变成目标，它就不再是一个好的度量。<bookmark mark='b'/>使劲推高点击，标题党就赢了；在它所代表的东西开始下降之后，指标还在继续上升。<bookmark mark='c'/>一个学习系统找到这个缺口，比任何人都快：这就是奖励投机，出自《人工智能，从零搭建》第31部分。<bookmark mark='d'/>防御的办法是：多个指标、护栏、长期保留组，以及去问用户。

eb1d4da295b5.en: A short-term number can also turn a product against its users. <bookmark mark='a'/> In 2010 the designer Harry Brignull named dark patterns: designs that trick people into doing what they did not mean to. <bookmark mark='b'/> One click to subscribe, six steps to leave. A box ticked in advance. A cost that appears at the last step. A refusal button that mocks you. <bookmark mark='c'/> And an experiment that counts only today's sign-ups will discover these by itself, and call each a win.
eb1d4da295b5.zh: 一个短期的数字，也可能让产品反过来对付它的用户。<bookmark mark='a'/>2010年，设计师 Harry Brignull 给暗黑模式（dark patterns）起了名字：诱骗人们去做他们本不想做的事情的设计。<bookmark mark='b'/>订阅只要点一下，退订要六步。一个预先勾好的框。一项到最后一步才出现的费用。一个嘲弄你的拒绝按钮。<bookmark mark='c'/>而一个只计算今天注册数的实验，会自己发现这些设计，并把每一个都算作胜利。

341909287142.en: Every A/B test is an experiment on people, usually a harmless one. <bookmark mark='a'/> In 2014 Adam Kramer, Jamie Guillory and Jeffrey Hancock reported that for one week in January 2012, about six hundred and eighty-nine thousand Facebook users had been shown fewer positive posts, or fewer negative ones. <bookmark mark='b'/> Their own posts shifted slightly the same way. <bookmark mark='c'/> The reaction was strong: no one had been asked, and the journal published an editorial expression of concern. <bookmark mark='d'/> The Belmont Report of 1979 asks research on people for respect for persons, beneficence and justice; few product tests meet an ethics board, but the principles apply. <bookmark mark='e'/> Measuring without watching anyone is for the frontier.
341909287142.zh: 每个 A/B 测试都是一次在人身上做的实验，通常是无害的。<bookmark mark='a'/>2014年，Adam Kramer、Jamie Guillory 和 Jeffrey Hancock 报告说，在 2012年1月的一周里，大约 68.9万名 Facebook 用户被展示了更少的正面帖子，或者更少的负面帖子。<bookmark mark='b'/>他们自己发的帖子，也朝同一个方向轻微偏移。<bookmark mark='c'/>反应很强烈：没有人被征求过意见，期刊发表了一份编辑部关注声明。<bookmark mark='d'/>1979年的《贝尔蒙报告》要求对人的研究做到尊重个人、有益和公正；很少有产品测试会经过伦理委员会，但这些原则同样适用。<bookmark mark='e'/>不监视任何人的测量，留给前沿一章。

d063f6e2913c.en: Chapter thirteen, the frontier. What can an experiment not see?
d063f6e2913c.zh: 第十三章，前沿：一个实验看不到什么？

3c5fce0cb8c9.en: Every test in this part assumed that what happens to one user does not depend on what happens to another. Marketplaces break that. <bookmark mark='a'/> We simulated ten thousand buyers and three thousand items. The treatment makes buyers six points keener. <bookmark mark='b'/> But supply is limited, so every extra item a treated buyer takes is one a control buyer cannot have. <bookmark mark='c'/> The A/B test reports a lift of 5.4 points. Launch the treatment to everyone, and sales rise by 0.2: almost nothing, because supply was the limit all along. With ample supply the two agree. <bookmark mark='d'/> The fixes randomize whole units that do not interact: entire cities, or alternating time slots, called switchbacks, and in social networks, clusters of friends, as Johan Ugander and colleagues proposed in 2013. Designing experiments under interference is an active field.
3c5fce0cb8c9.zh: 这一部分的每个测试都假设，一个用户身上发生的事，不取决于另一个用户身上发生的事。市场打破了这一点。<bookmark mark='a'/>我们模拟了一万名买家和三千件商品。处理让买家的购买意愿提高了六个百分点。<bookmark mark='b'/>但供给有限，所以实验组买家多拿走的每一件商品，都是对照组买家得不到的一件。<bookmark mark='c'/>A/B 测试报告的提升是 5.4 个百分点。把处理推给所有人，销量上升 0.2：几乎为零，因为限制从头到尾都是供给。供给充足时，两者一致。<bookmark mark='d'/>解决办法是把彼此不相互作用的整个单元随机化：整座城市，或者交替的时间段，称为轮换实验（switchback）；在社交网络里，则是朋友组成的聚类，这是 Johan Ugander 和同事在 2013年提出的。在干扰之下设计实验，是一个活跃的领域。

8f0deaf661be.en: A second limit is time. <bookmark mark='a'/> A test runs for two weeks; what a company cares about, whether people are still using the product next year, takes a year to see. Novelty fades, habits form, and a short test can point the wrong way. <bookmark mark='b'/> One answer is the surrogate index of Susan Athey, Raj Chetty, Guido Imbens and Hyunseung Kang: learn, from many past experiments, how short-term signals predict the long-term outcome, and use that prediction as the metric. <bookmark mark='c'/> Another is a long-running holdout: a few users kept on the old product for months, against whom the accumulated effect of many launches is measured. <bookmark mark='d'/> When a surrogate can be trusted, and how wrong it can be, are open questions.
8f0deaf661be.zh: 第二个限制是时间。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个测试跑两周；而公司关心的事，人们明年是否还在用这个产品，要一年才能看到。新奇感会消退，习惯会养成，一个短期测试可能指错方向。<bookmark mark='b'/>一个答案是 Susan Athey、Raj Chetty、Guido Imbens 和 Hyunseung Kang 的替代指数：从许多过去的实验中学习短期信号如何预测长期结果，再把这个预测当作指标。<bookmark mark='c'/>另一个答案是长期运行的保留组：让少数用户几个月都留在旧产品上，用他们来衡量许多次上线累积起来的效应。<bookmark mark='d'/>替代指标什么时候可信，它可能错多少，都还是开放问题。

76761804e759.en: A third limit is privacy: some things should be measured without anyone being watched. <bookmark mark='a'/> The oldest trick is Stanley Warner's randomized response, from 1965. Ask a sensitive question. Each person answers truthfully three times in four, and otherwise flips a coin and gives that answer instead. <bookmark mark='b'/> No single answer reveals anything certain, but the rate in the population can be recovered by undoing the known noise. <bookmark mark='c'/> The price is precision: with a true rate of twenty percent, the private estimate's error is about one and a half times that of an honest survey of the same size, at every size we tried. In today's language this is local differential privacy, with epsilon of about 1.9. <bookmark mark='d'/> Google's RAPPOR used it for browser statistics in 2014, Apple for keyboard statistics in 2016, and the 2020 United States Census applied differential privacy centrally to its published tables.
76761804e759.zh: 第三个限制是隐私：有些东西应当在不监视任何人的情况下测量。<bookmark mark='a'/>最古老的技巧，是 Stanley Warner 1965年提出的随机化回答。问一个敏感问题。每个人四次里有三次如实回答，其余时候就抛一枚硬币，改为给出硬币的答案。<bookmark mark='b'/>任何一个单独的答案都透露不出确定的信息，但只要撤销已知的噪声，就能还原总体中的比例。<bookmark mark='c'/>代价是精度：真实比例为 20% 时，私密估计的误差大约是同样规模的诚实调查的 1.5 倍，我们试过的每种规模都是如此。用今天的话说，这就是本地差分隐私，ε 大约是 1.9。<bookmark mark='d'/>2014年，Google 的 RAPPOR 用它来统计浏览器数据；2016年，Apple 用它来统计键盘数据；而 2020年的美国人口普查，则在中心化的层面上，对公布的表格应用了差分隐私。

997a1def4623.en: Finally, models. Fitts's and Hick's laws were the first models of people at computers, and research is building richer ones. <bookmark mark='a'/> Computational rationality treats a person as an agent making the best decisions it can under the limits of its perception and memory, and predicts pointing, typing and visual search from first principles. <bookmark mark='b'/> Simulated users let designers test an interface before anyone sees it, and language models are now tried as synthetic participants, with good reason for caution. <bookmark mark='c'/> And interfaces that adapt to each person raise their own question: when does adapting help, and when does it make a product unpredictable? <bookmark mark='d'/> Underneath all of them is one question: how far can prediction replace measurement?
997a1def4623.zh: 最后是模型。菲茨定律和希克定律，是最早的关于人在计算机前的模型，而研究正在构建更丰富的模型。<bookmark mark='a'/>计算理性把人看作一个智能体，在自身感知和记忆的限制下，尽可能做出最好的决策，并从第一性原理出发，预测指点、打字和视觉搜索。<bookmark mark='b'/>模拟用户让设计者在任何人看到界面之前就能测试它；语言模型现在也被尝试用作合成的参与者，而谨慎是有充分理由的。<bookmark mark='c'/>而针对每个人自适应的界面，带来了它们自己的问题：自适应什么时候有帮助，什么时候又会让产品变得不可预测？<bookmark mark='d'/>在所有这些下面，是同一个问题：预测在多大程度上能取代测量？

bd0ee20c8dfb.en: Open problems. <bookmark mark='a'/> Interference: experimental designs for marketplaces and social networks that are unbiased and still have the power to detect small effects. <bookmark mark='b'/> Long-term effects: knowing when short-term surrogates can be trusted, with bounds on how wrong they can be. <bookmark mark='c'/> Private experimentation: A/B tests under differential privacy at the smallest cost in power. <bookmark mark='d'/> And user models accurate enough to replace a first round of testing with people. <bookmark mark='e'/> This part's research problem joins two of this part's ideas: an always-valid sequential test for experiments with interference, whose error rate holds however often you look.
bd0ee20c8dfb.zh: 开放问题。<bookmark mark='a'/>干扰：为市场和社交网络设计的实验，既要无偏，又仍有足够的功效检测出小的效应。<bookmark mark='b'/>长期效应：知道短期替代指标什么时候可信，并给出它们可能错多少的界。<bookmark mark='c'/>私密的实验：在差分隐私下做 A/B 测试，而功效上的代价最小。<bookmark mark='d'/>以及足够准确的用户模型，能够取代第一轮真人测试。<bookmark mark='e'/>这一部分的研究题，把这一部分的两个想法结合起来：一个针对存在干扰的实验、始终有效的序贯检验，无论你看多少次，它的错误率都成立。

0e6a8c30b85b.en: What we built in this part. Fitts's law, out of a noisy channel of corrected movements, and Hick's law, out of the entropy of a choice. Predictions of task time from a few operators. Colour as formulas, and this series' own palette checked for contrast and for colour-blind viewers. The number of users a usability study needs, and why the famous five can be too few. The A/B test and its sample size, the false winners that come from looking every day, a sequential test that is safe to look at, and CUPED, which removes the variance a user's past already explains. One idea runs through it: people can be measured, but measuring them well takes the same care as any other experiment.
0e6a8c30b85b.zh: 我们在这一部分搭建了什么。菲茨定律，出自一条由一次次修正动作构成的噪声信道；希克定律，出自一次选择的熵。由几个操作符预测任务用时。把颜色当作公式，并检查了这个系列自己的调色板的对比度，以及它对色盲观众的效果。一项可用性研究需要多少用户，以及为什么著名的五个人可能太少。A/B 测试及其样本量，每天都看所带来的假赢家，一个可以放心去看的序贯检验，还有 CUPED，它去掉了用户的过去已经解释了的那部分方差。贯穿其中的是一个想法：人是可以测量的，但要测量得好，需要像对待任何其他实验一样小心。

bbec49e74d82.en: Where this comes back. Parts 45 and 50 run experiments on infrastructure itself, as canaries and staged rollouts. Part 46 builds the pipelines that log every event these experiments analyse. Part 47 ranks search results and measures whether the ranking helps. Part 51 draws glyphs and colour on the GPU. And Part 57 asks the deeper version of this part's statistical questions: when does what we measured on some people generalize to the rest?
bbec49e74d82.zh: 它们会在哪里再出现。第45和第50部分在基础设施本身上做实验，形式是金丝雀发布和分阶段上线。第46部分搭建流水线，记录这些实验所分析的每一个事件。第47部分给搜索结果排序，并测量排序是否有帮助。第51部分在 GPU 上绘制字形和颜色。而第57部分会提出这一部分统计问题的更深版本：我们在一些人身上测到的东西，什么时候能推广到其余的人？

7b7e010259fc.en: In practice. Make frequent targets big and close, and use the screen's edges and corners. Respond within a tenth of a second, show progress after a second, and let people do something else after ten. Give text a contrast of at least four and a half to one, never use colour as the only signal, and look at your design through a colour-blind simulation. Test with a few users, often, fixing what they find between rounds. And fix an experiment's sample size before it starts, or use a sequential test, and always check that the split is the one you asked for.
7b7e010259fc.zh: 实践中。把常用的目标做得又大又近，并利用屏幕的边和角。在十分之一秒内响应，过了一秒就显示进度，过了十秒就让人们可以去做别的事。文字的对比度至少要 4.5 比 1，永远不要把颜色当作唯一的信号，并且通过色盲模拟看看你的设计。用少数几个用户、经常测试，在两轮之间修好他们发现的问题。还有，在实验开始之前定好样本量，或者使用序贯检验，并且始终检查分组是不是你要求的那样。

9fbd31b83863.en: Six problems, with full solutions in the part's notes. Pause on any of them. The fifth is a build problem: correct for daily peeking the old-fashioned way, by dividing alpha among thirty looks, and compare its power with the sequential test. The last, marked with a star, is a research problem: a sequential test that stays valid when the people in an experiment affect each other.
9fbd31b83863.zh: 六道习题，完整的解答在这一部分的笔记里。可以在任何一道上暂停。第五道是一道动手题：用老办法纠正每天偷看的问题，把 α 分给三十次查看，再把它的功效与序贯检验相比较。最后一道，标着星号，是一道研究题：一个在实验中的人彼此影响时仍然有效的序贯检验。

938e2ba137a2.en: Next time, Part 45, and the start of Act Nine: the cloud. A modern application rents its computer by the second, from a building the size of a stadium. Underneath sit power and cooling budgets, virtual machines shrunk to micro-VMs, containers placed by bin packing, and control loops that keep making what is match what should be.
938e2ba137a2.zh: 下一次是第45部分，也是第九幕的开始：云。一个现代应用按秒租用它的计算机，计算机就在一座体育场那么大的建筑里。在下面是电力和冷却的预算，缩小成微虚拟机的虚拟机，用装箱算法放置的容器，以及不断让现状去符合应有状态的控制回路。

9bd24692775d.en: The books and papers this part follows are on screen and in the notes. Thank you for watching.
9bd24692775d.zh: 这一部分所依据的书和论文，列在屏幕上，也在笔记里。感谢收看。
